title: The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Chair
summary: Given a party with n friends and an infinite number of chairs numbered from 0 to infinity, each friend sits on the unoccupied chair with the smallest number upon arrival.
statement: Given a party with n friends and an infinite number of chairs numbered from 0 to infinity, each friend sits on the unoccupied chair with the smallest number upon arrival. If a friend leaves, their chair becomes available. You are provided with the arrival and departure times for each friend and a target friend. Determine the chair number the target friend will sit on.
constraints: times contains 2 through 10000 [arrival, leaving] pairs with distinct arrival times.
A chair freed at the same time as an arrival is immediately available; each arrival takes the smallest free chair.
hints: Two min-heaps track the earliest departures and the smallest currently free chair.
Process arrivals chronologically, release every chair whose departure is at most the arrival, then take the smallest available chair.
Sort (arrival, leaving, friend); pop expired occupied entries into available; pop one chair and stop when friend is target.
All and only free chairs are in the available heap at each arrival, so its minimum is the mandated assignment; stopping at the target cannot affect its chair.
editorial: All and only free chairs are in the available heap at each arrival, so its minimum is the mandated assignment; stopping at the target cannot affect its chair.

tests.explanation: Friend one arrives second and receives chair one.
At time three chairs zero and one are occupied, so the target receives chair two.
